name: Cascades d'Ouzoud
description: One of Morocco's tallest waterfalls, dropping around 110 meters in three tiers into the El-Abid River gorge, near the village of Tanaghmeilt in Azilal province. Surrounded by olive groves, with walking paths to the base, boat rides beneath the falls, and resident Barbary macaques along the trail.
hours: Open year-round, daylight hours; best visited morning or late afternoon
source: Google Maps verified

name: Ain Asserdoun
description: A natural spring and terraced garden park above Béni Mellal, around 640 meters altitude, with pools fed by cool spring water, cafés, and mule rides. A well-loved local spot for walks and picnics, with a path leading up to the hilltop kasbah.
hours: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM daily
source: Google Maps verified

name: Kasr Aïn Asserdoun
description: Hilltop fortress (Kasr / Kasbah Aïn Asserdoun) above the Aïn Asserdoun spring gardens in Béni Mellal, historically linked to the Moulay Ismail era. Panoramic views over the city and the Tadla plain; grounds sometimes host cultural events. Also known locally as Kasbah Ras el Aïn.
hours: Open year-round, exterior/grounds accessible; interior access varies
source: Google Maps verified

name: Lac et barrage de Bin El Ouidane
description: A large turquoise reservoir formed by a dam on the El Abid and Ahansal rivers in the Atlas Mountains, roughly 132 meters high and 290 meters wide. Popular for boating, fishing, jet skiing, and scenic drives.
hours: Open year-round, daylight hours
source: Google Maps verified

name: Kasbah Tadla
description: A historic town on the Oum Er-Rbia river, along the old Fes-Marrakech caravan route, with a walled medina and ramparts from its time as a strategic military post.
hours: Medina open year-round, daylight hours
source: Google Maps verified

name: Imi n'Ifri Natural Bridge
description: A massive natural limestone arch near Demnate, formed by a collapsed underground cave system, with the Mehasseur river running through the gorge below. A short, adventurous hike leads under and through the bridge. Classified as a site of biological and ecological interest.
hours: Closed Mondays; open 24 hours other days
source: Google Maps verified

name: Khenifra National Park
description: A protected area in the Middle Atlas spanning cedar and oak forests, part of the Atlas Cedar Biosphere Reserve, with high-altitude lakes (Aguelmame Sidi Ali, Aguelmame Azigza), hiking trails, and wildlife including Barbary macaques.
hours: Open year-round; best access spring through autumn
source: approximate - large protected area, verify exact boundary before use

name: Aguelmame Azigza (Aziza)
description: A karstic high-altitude lake also called Aguelmame Aziza — the 'green lake' — surrounded by cedar and pine forest within Khenifra National Park. Popular for camping and swimming, with occasional deer sightings.
hours: Open year-round; camping possible around the lake
source: Google Maps verified

name: Khenifra Waterfall Park
description: A small, recently restored waterfall and landscaped park at the entrance to Khenifra city, with benches and gardens - popular for a short evening walk rather than a full excursion.
hours: Open 24 hours
source: Google Maps verified

name: Gorges de Taghzirte
description: Oak-forested canyons about 20 km from Beni Mellal, carved by the Aqqa-n-Ouhansal and Oued Derna rivers, with caves and rock shelters still used seasonally by shepherds. A roughly 5-hour hiking route.
hours: Daylight hours; guide recommended for the full route
source: approximate - verify exact trailhead coordinates

name: Vallee des Ait Bouguemez
description: Known as the 'happy valley,' a green plateau at 1,800-2,400m in the central High Atlas, dotted with traditional ochre pise villages and terraced fields, at the foot of Mount M'Goun. Part of the UNESCO M'Goun Geopark. Reference point: Souk Tabant, the valley's main weekly market.
hours: Villages accessible year-round; some passes affected by winter snow
source: Google Maps verified (Souk Tabant reference point)

name: Zaouiat Ahansal
description: A High Atlas village and hiking/canyoning base within the M'Goun Geopark, known for access to dramatic gorge scenery including the rock formation locally called 'La Cathedrale.'
hours: Open year-round; best accessed spring through autumn
source: Google Maps verified

name: Greniers d'Aoujgal (Tihouna n'Aoujgal)
description: Traditional communal granaries built into cliffside terrain from stone and rammed earth - a distinctive regional architectural heritage sometimes described as one of the world's oldest collective storage systems. Dramatic clifftop scenery.
hours: Open year-round, daylight hours
source: Google Maps verified

name: Sources de l’Oum Er-Rbia
description: Headwaters of Morocco’s Oum Er-Rbia river in the Middle Atlas near Khénifra, with dozens of freshwater and mineral springs cascading from limestone cliffs. A classic picnic and short-walk site inside the wider Aguelmame Azigza / cedar-forest landscape.
hours: Open year-round, daylight hours
source: Wikimapia / regional tourism references (33°3′10″N 5°24′50″W)

name: Sources Zaouiat Cheikh / Parc Tamda
description: Mountain spring complex and landscaped water park near Zaouiat Cheikh (Béni Mellal province), fed by clear natural springs — popular for family outings and weekend recreation.
hours: Typically daylight hours; facilities may vary by season
source: Nominatim town center Zaouiat Cheikh — verify park entrance on site

name: Parc de Taghbalout (El Ksiba)
description: Shaded pine and cedar setting around natural freshwater pools near Dir El Ksiba / Taghbalout — a cooler escape for walks and picnics in the foothills.
hours: Open year-round, daylight hours
source: Nominatim Taghbalout, RN12 / Dir El Ksiba

name: Assif Ahansal (river corridor)
description: Major High Atlas mountain river corridor used for white-water kayaking, rafting, riverside camping, and approaches into Zaouiat Ahansal country. Conditions depend heavily on season and water levels — go with local operators.
hours: Seasonal outdoor access; guide recommended for water sports
source: Nominatim Assif Ahansal near Zaouiat Ahansal

name: Aïn Kbi (Fquih Ben Salah)
description: Quiet natural spring oasis with palm shade on the Tadla plain near Fquih Ben Salah — a local picnic and refreshment stop rather than a major tourist complex.
hours: Daylight hours
source: approximate — near Fquih Ben Salah; confirm spring access locally

name: Aguelmame Sidi Ali
description: High-altitude volcanic / karst lake on the Khénifra–Ifrane side of the Middle Atlas, known for tranquil mountain scenery and birdwatching. Cooler climate; pack layers.
hours: Open year-round; best late spring to autumn
source: Nominatim Lac Aguelmame Sidi Ali

name: Lacs de Tigelmamine / Ouiouane
description: Twin natural lakes in the Middle Atlas forest near Oum Rabia / Aguelmous country — often nicknamed the “eyes” of the Khénifra highlands. Quiet setting for walks and photography.
hours: Open year-round, daylight hours
source: Nominatim Lac Ouiouane (Tigelmamine twin-lakes area)

name: Lac Tamda (Azilal / Anmiter area)
description: High-altitude alpine lake in the Azilal High Atlas, typically reached by scenic trekking paths near Anmiter / Aït Bouguemez approaches. Remote — plan daylight returns.
hours: Daylight; trek access only in good weather
source: approximate — High Atlas lake near Aït Bouguemez approaches; verify trailhead

name: Jebel M’Goun (Ighil M’Goun)
description: One of the High Atlas’s ultra-prominent summits at about 4,071 m — a multi-day trekking objective from the M’Goun / Aït Bouguemez side. Requires mountain experience or a certified guide.
hours: Seasonal mountaineering; summer–early autumn preferred
source: Wikipedia / Peaklist coordinates

name: Cathédrale d’Imsfrane (Amsafrane)
description: Massive sheer rock wall near Tilougguite / Ouawizeght country, often compared to a gothic cathedral façade. Popular for hiking viewpoints and climbing with local partners.
hours: Daylight; climbing only with qualified guides
source: Nominatim Cathédrale d’Imsfrane (Amsafrane)

name: Gorges de Tissilit
description: Dramatic river canyon in Azilal province used for canyoning, climbing, and wild scenery day trips. Access and difficulty vary with water levels — hire local canyon guides.
hours: Seasonal; guide strongly recommended
source: approximate — Azilal canyon country near Ahansal approaches

name: Vallées d’Ahouli & Mibladen
description: Rugged red-rock gorges and former mining settlements on the Midelt side of the Atlas, historically linked to regional lead/silver mining. Photogenic canyons; check road conditions.
hours: Daylight; remote roads
source: Nominatim Aouli / Mibladen (Midelt border of the wider region)

name: Empreintes de dinosaures d’Iouaridène
description: Famous Jurassic dinosaur trackways in red continental sandstones near Demnate, within the M’Goun UNESCO Global Geopark — theropod and sauropod prints protected with walkways and panels.
hours: Daylight; stay on marked paths to protect the prints
source: Geopark / scientific literature approximate site location near Demnate

name: Plis / formations de Mastfrane (Tillouguit)
description: Striking folded sedimentary rock layers visible in the Tillouguit / Ouawizeght foothills — a roadside and short-hike geology highlight of the Central High Atlas.
hours: Daylight viewpoints
source: approximate — near Imsfrane / Tillouguit geology corridor

name: Kasbah Bel-Kush (Fquih Ben Salah)
description: Historic citadel associated with 18th-century trade-route defenses on the Tadla plain at Fquih Ben Salah. Exterior viewing is the usual visit; interior access may be limited.
hours: Exterior year-round; interior access varies
source: approximate — Fquih Ben Salah urban kasbah; confirm access

name: Kasbah Moha ou Hammou Zayani (Khénifra)
description: Historic Amazigh stronghold in Khénifra linked to resistance leader Moha ou Hammou Zayani. Part of the city’s heritage circuit along the Oum Er-Rbia corridor.
hours: Exterior accessible; guided visits when available
source: approximate — Khénifra historic kasbah district

name: Agadir n’Aït Bouguemez (Sidi Chita)
description: Hilltop fortified communal granary (agadir) overlooking the Happy Valley, with wide 360° views over terraced fields and villages. Combine with a valley cultural walk.
hours: Daylight; ask locally before entering private compounds
source: approximate — Sidi Chita / Aït Bouguemez granary viewpoints

name: Zaouia de Sidi Hamza (Azilal)
description: Traditional spiritual center in the Azilal Atlas, historically associated with scholarship and manuscript heritage. Visit respectfully; photography rules may apply.
hours: Respect prayer times; ask permission to enter
source: approximate — Azilal Atlas zaouia; confirm village approach

name: Plateau d’Ajdir & cédraie
description: High Middle Atlas forest plateau of Atlas cedar and oak near the Khénifra–Azrou approaches, habitat for Barbary macaques. Cool air; great for scenic drives and short forest walks.
hours: Daylight; watch for livestock and wildlife on roads
source: approximate — Ajdir / Oum Rabia forest plateau corridor

name: Parc El Ochaq (Khénifra)
description: Central landscaped city park in Khénifra with streams, plantings, and local gathering spaces — a soft urban break between mountain day trips.
hours: Typically open daytime; evenings vary
source: approximate — Khénifra city park (Parc El Ochaq / Lovers’ Park)

name: Khouribga — patrimoine minier des phosphates
description: Industrial and cultural landscape of Morocco’s phosphate industry around Khouribga, with open-pit heritage and urban visitor points that explain the region’s mining story. Pair with local museums / guided industry visits when available.
hours: Urban sites vary; industrial zones are restricted
source: Nominatim Khouribga — do not enter active mine sites

name: Lac / parc central d’Oued Zem
description: Historic city park organized around a large artificial lake created in the early 20th century — a local leisure landmark between Khouribga and the Tadla corridor.
hours: Daytime public access
source: Nominatim Rue de Lac, Oued Zem

name: Marché central & vieux quartier (Béni Mellal)
description: Vibrant central market and old-quarter streets of Béni Mellal for regional spices, olive oil, citrus, and traditional textiles. Go early; bargain politely; keep valuables secure in crowds.
hours: Morning peak; many stalls close midday Friday prayer
source: approximate — Béni Mellal central market / medina district

name: Musée d’Azilal (Géoparc M’Goun)
description: National museums network site in Azilal dedicated to earth sciences and the M’Goun UNESCO Global Geopark. Circular “Temple of Knowledge” trail with fossils, minerals, regional biodiversity, and the Atlasaurus dinosaur display. Address: Avenue Hassan II, administrative quarter, Azilal.
hours: Check FNM / local hours — typically daytime; closed some Mondays
source: FNM Musée d’Azilal — Avenue Hassan II, Azilal

name: CIP / Musée d’Aïn Asserdoun
description: Centre d’Interprétation du Patrimoine in the Aïn Asserdoun gardens (Béni Mellal): digital and physical exhibits on regional nature, archaeology, Amazigh architecture (igherman), crafts, costumes, and performing arts (Ahwach / Ahidous). Pair with the terraced spring gardens just outside.
hours: Daytime museum hours; ticketed — check ministry culture e-services
source: Ministère de la Culture — CIP Ain Assardoun (approx. garden complex)

name: Espace de la Mémoire (Résistance & Libération) — Béni Mellal
description: Local history museum dedicated to the region’s role in Morocco’s resistance and independence struggle, with photographs, documents, and artifacts. A focused cultural stop in Béni Mellal city.
hours: Weekday daytime hours — confirm locally before visiting
source: approximate — Béni Mellal urban cultural district

name: Maison du Géoparc — Aït Bouguemez
description: Geopark visitor house in the Happy Valley: orientation to M’Goun geosites, local culture, and hiking options. Useful first stop before multi-day treks in Aït Bouguemez.
hours: Seasonal / daytime — ask in Tabant or at the house
source: M’Goun Geopark houses network — Aït Bouguemez (approx. valley center)

name: Maison du Géoparc — Zaouiat Ahansal
description: Geopark interpretation house serving the Ahansal corridor: canyon access info, village heritage, and trail orientation for visitors exploring gorges and climbing areas.
hours: Seasonal / daytime — confirm on arrival
source: M’Goun Geopark houses — Zaouiat Ahansal (approx.)

name: Maison du Géoparc — Iouaridène
description: Geopark house near the famous dinosaur trackways of Iouaridène (Demnate side): context for Jurassic footprints and responsible visiting of geosites.
hours: Daytime when staffed — combine with the trackway visit
source: M’Goun Geopark houses — Iouaridène (approx. near trackways)

name: Parc municipal de Béni Mellal
description: Central urban green space in Béni Mellal for evening walks, family outings, and a soft break between heritage and mountain day trips. Shaded paths and local gathering spots.
hours: Open year-round, typically daylight to evening
source: approximate — Béni Mellal city park / public garden area

name: Vergers & oliveraies périurbaines (Béni Mellal)
description: Olive grove belts surrounding Béni Mellal that act as informal green parks — cool walks and rural scenery at the foot of the Middle Atlas, especially pleasant in late afternoon.
hours: Daylight; respect private orchard access
source: approximate — olive belt southwest of Béni Mellal

name: Jardins botaniques d’Aïn Asserdoun
description: Terraced botanical gardens around the Aïn Asserdoun spring complex: roses, fruit trees, shaded picnic lawns, and paths linking the spring pools to the hilltop kasbah and CIP museum.
hours: Aligned with Ain Asserdoun garden access (often 9:00–17:00)
source: Aïn Asserdoun garden complex — distinct from the spring pools POI
